Breathing on the beat

One in-out breath per beat; quick in, slow out means a short inhale and a long exhale. The teacher can adjust the tempo.

6573990d22: **Diphthongs**: rhymes made of two or more vowels, such as \[ai\] in 愛 and 唉 or \[au\] in 熬, with the weight on the second vowel. On a long note, hold the first vowel, then close clearly on the second at the end so listeners can tell which word it is.
2d080b102d: **Nasal finals**: -an and -en close on the tongue tip (front nasal n), -ang and -eng on the back of the tongue (back nasal ng). If the endings of 心 and 星, or 情 and 勤, blur together, people will mishear the lyrics.
8bfb20c296: Extended notes: scales and staccato chord exercises
c4b0f49c34: **Exercise 1: basic scale exercise**. Play the audio: the piano plays a C major octave at 70 BPM, and you sing along with the melody and rhythm on \[a\], \[i\], \[u\], \[e\], \[o\] in turn. Sing standing up, and always fill up with breath before each cycle.
b856cd764f: **Exercise 2: staccato chord exercise**. One cycle is the diatonic chords of C major, again sung on each of the five vowels. Staccato means "short, crisp, strong" detached notes; push every note out with a bounce from the belly, using the same muscles as "quick in, quick out" from Lesson 2.
2f86768824: Staccato is common in fast songs, syncopation and ragtime-style rhythms, so it's a must. Guitarists can play the seven chords as arpeggios themselves and sing while playing, training pitch and sense of harmony together.
bb0bb81fce: Consonants usually come before vowels. The rule is "consonants short and clear, vowels long and round": consonants make you understood, vowels make you sound good.
a9b4d2fca8: Tongue tip against the back of the lower teeth
a26f90388c: Tongue tip curls up toward the hard palate, just far enough, not too much
3bbd868ddf: A palm in front of your mouth feels the air when you say them; ease off a little in front of a microphone to avoid popping
0dff7cff81: Almost no airflow, light and neat
0e125964f1: Consonants rarely stand alone; they mostly show up in fast songs or advertising jingles, like the well-known Taiwanese cold-syrup jingle. Practise consonants the same way as vowels; after about a month your resonance will change, with fuller low notes and rounder high notes.

67dd1f483c: This song rhymes on \[i\], so sing it all on the /i/ vowel and focus on whether resonance and breath stay connected.
3c26b91692: Finally bring in the lyrics, adding diction only on the consonants and keeping the vowels as round as in step two.
aca79ca3a4: **Handling the rhymes**: the chorus lines "不是因為天氣晴朗才愛你／不是因為看見星星才想你" all rhyme on \[i\]. The long note on 你 tends to go flat, so keep the corners of the mouth slightly spread and the jaw relaxed, with the yawning space still inside. 星星 and 晴朗 are back nasals (-eng/-ang) and close on the back of the tongue.

Ending a long note

Hold the vowel first, then close clearly: 愛 moves from a to i, 心 closes on n with the tongue tip, 星 closes on ng with the back of the tongue. When to close can follow the demo.
